video_title: NEAR Just Turned Staking Yield Into Compute
gist: NEAR co-founder Ilia explains a new token mechanic in which staked NEAR redirects staking yield to pay compute providers, giving holders a proportional allowance of confidential, verifiable AI inference on the NEAR AI Cloud instead of a fiat subscription. The conversation extends into NEAR's vertically integrated stack (blockchain, confidential intents, NEAR AI Cloud, Ironclaw agents), the case for autonomous businesses that hold NEAR as an intelligence treasury, and why an opaque, non-storable GPU compute market is the next thing NEAR wants to make tradable via intents.

themes.theme: Staking Yield as an Inference Subscription

insights.claim: NEAR holders can now stake NEAR to receive AI inference on the NEAR AI Cloud instead of a fiat or per-token subscription, with the staking yield they forgo acting as the payment for the compute — a design Ilia calls 'universal basic AI' for holders and their agents.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Turns NEAR from a pure yield asset into a prepaid compute claim, so demand for inference becomes a direct sink for staked supply rather than a fee stream.
insights.quote: So the way it works is you effectively trading off your yield right the yield you can be generating on near is now being paid for the AI inference and and capacity under the hood.

insights.claim: The inference allowance from NEAR staking is metered strictly in proportion to stake size, so subscription-tier usage requires staking a correspondingly large NEAR position.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Creates a mechanical link between desired AI throughput and locked NEAR, meaning heavy agent users must scale their token position rather than their credit card spend.
insights.quote: Correct. Yeah. Yeah. It's exactly like proportional to how much you stake. And you know, if you want like a subscription level, you need to stake like in clips.

insights.claim: NEAR AI Cloud currently runs mostly on NEAR's own GPUs, bootstrapping supply itself before opening the network to third-party compute providers who will be paid out of staker-generated yield.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Supply is centralized today, so the decentralization and SLA quality of the third-party GPU marketplace is the key execution risk to track.
insights.quote: So right now we've been mostly having our own GPUs on this but we do have kind of underlying market that we've been developing so that other third parties can join as well.

insights.claim: Staked NEAR also unlocks Ironclaw, NEAR's agentic harness, as a full coding-and-workflow agent comparable to a Claude Code or Codex subscription, with organizations able to pay in dollars instead.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Puts NEAR in direct product competition with mainstream AI coding subscriptions, giving the token a usage benchmark investors can price against known SaaS ARR.

themes.theme: Confidentiality and Verifiability as the Product

insights.claim: NEAR AI Cloud sells two properties — end-to-end confidential inference and verifiability — returning a signed attestation whose chain of provenance covers the model hash, the exact prompt, the output, the specific GPU and the specific Intel CPU, though it relies on trusted execution environments and therefore on trusting hardware manufacturers.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: The provenance receipt is what makes inference usable inside financial contracts, but the trust root is hardware rather than math — a bounded risk shared with every TEE-based competitor.

insights.claim: Ilia argues the largest under-appreciated attack surface in AI is the closed-source system prompt of a major provider, which a single employee could modify to steer the beliefs of a billion users without detection.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Frames verifiable inference as a governance and political-risk hedge, not just a privacy feature — the strongest argument for regulated buyers to demand attestation.
insights.quote: if you want to manipulate a billion people right now into believing something the easiest way is to get a job in open AI and and modify the system prompt

insights.claim: NEAR serves open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Gemma) unmodified and applies no provider-level filtering, so outputs are only as uncensored as the underlying model's own training, with custom model uploads on the roadmap.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Caps how far the 'uncensored AI' pitch can go today and makes NEAR a pure distribution layer whose margins depend on open-weight models staying free and good.
insights.quote: it's as uncensored as a model so we are serving openweight models right so deep seats and GLMs uh and and uh kind of you know gemma etc so whatever is in that model you get that right

themes.theme: NEAR Token Value Capture and Distribution

insights.claim: Ilia's summary thesis is that NEAR is 'AI money': a store of value that simultaneously grants AI access via staking and captures transaction volume via intents, secured by its own block space.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: This is the value-capture pitch investors will be underwriting: a hybrid of monetary premium plus fee-driven buyback, distinct from pure block-space chains like Ethereum.
insights.quote: The overall is like this is AI money, right?

insights.claim: The revenue.near.org dashboard shows roughly 20-50% of NEAR emissions being captured and burned by the protocol, sourced from NEAR Intents plus base blockchain activity.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: A concrete, publicly trackable offset to inflation — the single best metric for judging whether the AI story converts into net token sink.

insights.claim: NEAR reached product-market fit for Intents through 2025 and only switched fees on in February 2026, and Ilia expects the same monetization sequence for NEAR AI — but with staking arriving first as the primitive.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Sets an explicit playbook and timeline: expect fee activation on NEAR AI only after usage scales, so near-term revenue will be understated versus adoption.
insights.quote: we got to product market fit through 2025 and then we turned on the fees in February 26 we expect similar thing happening with uh near AI

insights.claim: Ilia concedes there is an unresolved accounting problem in equating staking-based inference access with protocol revenue, since it produces value as forgone yield rather than direct payment.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Standard revenue multiples will misread NEAR's AI business; analysts need a yield-diversion metric, and headline revenue dashboards may understate real economic throughput.

insights.claim: NEAR AI Cloud is being white-labeled by consumer-facing privacy brands including Venice and Brave, with Brave alone reporting over 100 million users.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Distribution through existing privacy-brand user bases is the fastest path to inference volume without NEAR owning consumer acquisition costs.

insights.claim: Announced NEAR AI Cloud customers include the government of Bermuda for citizen financial and pension guidance, and Abound, a US-to-India remittance product that also uses NEAR's stablecoin payments infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Government and regulated-finance logos validate the confidentiality pitch and suggest the sales motion is enterprise/public sector, not crypto-native retail.

themes.theme: Autonomous Businesses and the Agent Economy

insights.claim: Ilia's design target is 'autonomous businesses' that run 24/7, hold NEAR on the balance sheet as a non-depleting source of intelligence, transact on-chain, and can be steered by token holders voting on mission and rules.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Positions NEAR as a treasury asset for agents rather than a payment rail — a demand source that grows with agent count, not with human user count.

insights.claim: An agent funded by depleting AI credits eventually loses intelligence and cannot recover, which is why Ilia argues an autonomous business needs a yield-bearing intelligence endowment rather than a prepaid balance.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: The clearest economic rationale for the staking model: it converts inference from an operating expense into a perpetual endowment, a genuinely novel financing structure for agents.
insights.quote: you need a monetization way to do this, right? Which doesn't deplete your uh your treasury, right, as an agent to actually run this intelligence.

insights.claim: NEAR smart contracts can pause a transaction, call AI inference, and resume with the model's response, so a token transfer can be conditioned on model output — which only works because the inference is verifiable end to end.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: A capability no general-purpose L1 offers; watch for insurance settlement and conditional-payment applications as the first real usage of it.
insights.quote: you can actually call an AI inference out of your smart contract because the transaction can actually pause wait for AI inference and unpause the transaction and continue

insights.claim: Ironclaw 1.0 has launched and Ilia claims it is the only multi-tenant agent system, isolating each user while keeping an organization on a single shared instance.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Multi-tenancy with isolation is the specific technical wedge for enterprise agent deployments, where per-user agent sprawl is the current blocker.
insights.quote: we're as far as I know the only multi-tenant agent system because we can actually isolate every user

insights.claim: Ilia describes the underlying GPU compute market as a complete disaster — opaque, dominated by bilateral cloud deal-making, with no one able to see actual supply, which he ties directly to why the market is pricing AI bubble risk.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Argues the AI bubble debate is an information problem, not a demand problem — transparency infrastructure would compress the risk premium on compute-exposed equities.
insights.quote: the compute compute market underneath right now is a complete disaster right it's it's a very opaque every cloud is like you know deal making left and right

insights.claim: Compute is a uniquely hard commodity because it combines oil's quality heterogeneity with electricity's non-storability, which is why the market defaults to multi-year bilateral contracts.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Explains why order books fail for compute and why any credible compute exchange must solve underspecified matching rather than price discovery alone.
insights.quote: It has properties of oil meaning like there's you know million different qual qualities that matter and then it also has property of electricity because you cannot store it

insights.claim: NEAR's approach to a compute market, demoed as an MVP at NEARCON, uses intents rather than an order book: a buyer posts an underspecified request (for example a thousand GPUs of a given spec) that solvers fill by sourcing capacity worldwide, with verifiable and often non-custodial delivery of actual inference or SSH access, creating liquidity for GPU hours themselves.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: A differentiated market design versus tokenized-compute order books; if solvers can price heterogeneous GPU lots, NEAR captures fees on the largest emerging commodity market.

insights.claim: The host predicts the AI compute secondary marketplace will be one of the dominant market narratives for the end of 2026 and the start of 2027.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: A timing call on narrative rotation — early positioning in compute-market infrastructure tokens ahead of that attention shift.

themes.theme: Open-Weight Economics and the SaaS Apocalypse Debate

insights.claim: The host argues Chinese open-weight releases delivering roughly 95% of frontier quality at about 5% of the cost reopen the question of where value accrues in the AI stack, benefiting inference distributors like NEAR AI and Venice that never pay training costs.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: If training economics stay unrecoverable, margin migrates to serving and verification layers — a structural argument for inference infrastructure over model labs.

insights.claim: Ilia expects computing to collapse into an AI operating system where agents generate software on the fly, bypass web pages, and block ads client-side — but says he is consistently too optimistic on timing and that human attachment to specific apps may slow it.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: A direct threat model for ad-supported web and app businesses; Cloudflare's agent-monetization push is the market's early defensive response.

insights.claim: Ilia frames the software shift as a scale flip: expensive development forced lowest-common-denominator products for mass distribution, whereas cheap generation lets each user get a bespoke interface, so incumbents may end up distributing only a 'recipe' rather than an app.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: Reframes the SaaS threat as disaggregation of the interface rather than replacement of the vendor — relevant to how seat-based software is valued.

insights.claim: Ilia's key caveat on AI-generated software is that producing bad software is now easy while reaching high quality remains hard, which is the gating factor on the SaaS-replacement thesis.
insights.speaker: Ilia (Near co-founder)
insights.so_what: The quality gap is the durable moat for incumbent SaaS; multiple compression may run ahead of actual churn, as no one has cancelled Salesforce yet.
insights.quote: developing a shitty software is easy. getting it to really high quality is still pretty hard.
